insight: Spot gold traded around $4,010 an ounce on 26 Oct, after a fall of about 4% in the week to 23 Oct, its steepest weekly drop since June.
Gold's record high is $5,589.38 an ounce, set on 28 Jan 2026.
The Fed decides on 28 Oct and is widely expected to hold. Traders put about a 75% chance on a rate hike by December, per CME FedWatch.
Brent crude was near $115 a barrel on 23 Oct, close to a five-month high, as tanker attacks slowed traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.
The EIA's October outlook has Brent averaging $105 a barrel in Q4 2026, $14 above its September forecast.
source: US EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook, via OilMonster

insight: US CPI rose 3.7% year on year in September, and the 10-year Treasury yield was near 5%.
Silver fell about 6% on 23 Oct to near $54 an ounce.
Silver first passed $60 an ounce in Dec 2025 and stayed above it in Sep 2026. Its previous major high was $49.82, in April 2011.
Kitco's weekly gold survey on 23 Oct: of 17 Wall Street analysts, 7 were bearish for the week ahead, 4 bullish and 6 neutral. Of 161 retail votes, 42% were bullish.
Adrian Day expects gold to hold $4,000 or break only slightly lower. Sean Lusk of Walsh Trading says the Iran conflict is capping any rally.
Central banks bought a net 289 tonnes of gold in Q2 2026, up 62% from a year earlier. Investment in gold ETFs, bars and coins was 262 tonnes.

Singapore jewellery volumes fell 8% year on year in Q3 2025, and the Singapore Jewellers Association president said GST exemption on investment-grade gold bars is pushing buyers to bullion over jewellery.

Year-end 2026 gold targets set in early 2026: Goldman Sachs $5,400, JPMorgan $6,300, UBS $6,200, Morgan Stanley about $4,800, HSBC range $3,950 to $5,050. Set when gold was near $4,870, so check for revisions before quoting.
Gold is far below its January record, so first-time buyers are asking if it is a good time to buy. Answer calmly: spread buying over time, premiums over spot still apply, no timing calls.
Gold fell this week while oil and conflict risk rose. A plain explainer on why rate hike fears and high yields pressure gold more than war headlines lift it is a strong market context angle.
Tie market posts to something a buyer can do: DCA, trade-in timing, premium over spot, storage. Avoid forecasts the shop would have to defend.
